First, the degree

How she got here

The road, in four stops

2023
First studio — SeptemberA reading room for the Harborview library. Her model fell over twice; the idea didn’t.
2024
The bridge — MayA footbridge over the canal at 1:50 scale, built with Marcus. It is, technically, still standing.
2026
The thesis — November“A Library That Stays Open” — a night library for shift workers, defended in the last week of November.
2027
The degree — 22 MayBachelor of Architecture, with honours. The tassel moves in the morning; this party is the evening.

Finding us

The Foundry Garden

214 Grand Street, Brooklyn, NY 11211

A walled garden behind the old foundry — enter through the green gate under the string lights. The L train to Bedford Avenue stops four minutes away; street parking on Grand and Driggs.

Open in Maps

The garden holds 80 seats — when they are gone, they are gone, so the RSVP below really counts.

Gifts, gently

The next chapter fund

Lisbon, from June

In June, Maya moves to Lisbon for her first architecture job. Instead of things, the family keeps a Next Chapter Fund — it buys the plane ticket, the deposit on a small flat, and a desk under a window. Every contribution is written into the yearbook’s last page.

Good questions

Before you ask Priya

Is this the graduation ceremony?

No — the ceremony is that morning at the university, tickets limited by the school. This is the celebration: dinner, the toast, and the toss, with room for everyone.

What does garden formal mean?

Long or midi dresses, jackets without ties. One warning from the family: the lawn eats stilettos — block heels or wedges will serve you better.

Can I bring my children?

Teenagers, gladly. The garden is an evening place and the guest list is the 80 seats, so little ones are better celebrated at the family brunch on Sunday.

Who is hosting?

Daniel & Priya Chen, Maya’s parents. Every reply on this page lands on their list — they are the ones counting the chairs.
